issues.description: The assignment and UML consistently use the class name "Meal" (e.g., SealSaloon has orders: Meal[] and methods taking Meal), but the template repository instead provides a fully implemented class named "Order" with the same structure (name + ingredients) and leaves Meal.java empty. This creates a naming conflict that can block students (tests will likely expect Meal) and forces them to guess whether to rename Order, duplicate it as Meal, or implement Meal separately.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement by removing Order.java and providing a proper Meal.java skeleton/implementation (name, ingredients, constructor, getters), or rename Order.java to Meal.java (including class/constructor name) and update Main.java/template references accordingly.

issues.description: The UML for Stock lists only inventory-related methods (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock), but the template Stock class exposes a public setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) method, allowing wholesale replacement of the inventory array. This undermines the intended encapsulation/design where stock contents should be managed via Stock/SealSaloon operations rather than replacing the internal array directly.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove setStockIngredients from the student-facing template, or reduce its visibility (e.g., package-private) and explicitly document it as a Main-only/testing helper not part of the required UML API.
